n6281417974: Weldon Spring hides one of the strangest stories on our whole drive. In World War Two the Army needed explosives, so it bought this land and moved out three little towns: Howell, Hamburg and Toonerville. They became the Weldon Spring Ordnance Works, a giant TNT factory. Later the site processed uranium. The cleanup took years, and all that waste was sealed inside a huge rock-covered hill, about seventy-five feet tall and as big as thirty football fields. Here's the fun twist: there are stairs to the top, and families climb it for the view. Most of the old factory land is now the Busch and Weldon Spring conservation areas, full of deer, lakes and trails, and the old waste-truck road is now a hiking path with signs for the vanished towns.
